svg.title: rope shapes
svg.text: 1.6 RoPE on one head: rotate_half, two products, one sum
q_rot = q · cos + rotate_half(q) · sin; the same happens for every head of q and k
halves swapped; the moved-left half flips sign
row p = position p; column i: angle p·θᵢ
(the two halves hold the same 32 angles)
element-wise: same shape in, same out
Why it is a rotation: feature i and feature i + 32 form a pair (x1ᵢ, x2ᵢ).
Column i of the output: x1ᵢ·cos − x2ᵢ·sin. Column i + 32: x2ᵢ·cos + x1ᵢ·sin.
That is the pair turned by angle p·θᵢ. Pair 0 turns fast (θ₀ = 1 rad per position); pair 31 barely moves.
Heads: cos and sin are [N, 64]; .unsqueeze(1) makes them [N, 1, 64], which
stretches over all 32 q heads ([N, 32, 64]) and all 8 k heads. Every head gets
the same rotation per position. v is NOT rotated.
animated: halves swap (rotate_half), each copy meets its cos / sin table, the two products slide together and add
